name: Gemariah
interpretive_note: Jeremiah 29:3 names his father only as Hilkiah. This site's genealogy follows its source data in linking him to the high priest Hilkiah of Josiah's reign; others have suggested Jeremiah's own father, Hilkiah of the priests at Anathoth (Jeremiah 1:1). Scripture does not say which Hilkiah is meant. He is a different man from Gemariah son of Shaphan, whose chamber is named in Jeremiah 36.
source_summary: One of two envoys King Zedekiah sent to Nebuchadnezzar in Babylon, who carried Jeremiah's letter to the exiles telling them to settle there and seek the city's welfare (Jeremiah 29:3).
family_friendly_summary: Gemariah was one of two messengers King Zedekiah sent from Jerusalem to the king of Babylon. On the same trip he carried a letter from the prophet Jeremiah to the people of Judah who had already been taken away as captives to Babylon. The letter told them to build houses, plant gardens, and pray for the city where they now lived, because God would bring them home after seventy years.
adult_story: Gemariah son of Hilkiah appears once in Scripture, as one of two envoys King Zedekiah of Judah sent to Nebuchadnezzar in Babylon (Jeremiah 29:3). Jeremiah used the journey to send a letter, carried by Gemariah and his companion Elasah son of Shaphan, to the elders, priests, prophets, and people who had already been taken into exile (29:1-3). The letter told the exiles to build houses, plant gardens, marry, and seek the welfare of the city where they had been carried, praying to the LORD on its behalf (29:4-7). It warned them not to listen to prophets promising a quick return (29:8-9), because the LORD would bring them home only after seventy years were completed for Babylon (29:10). Scripture records nothing else about Gemariah; his one recorded task was carrying God's word to His people far from home.
